questions.question: Which recurrence follows directly from the product definition for $n\geq 1$?
questions.explanation: The recurrence is n! = n * (n-1)! (splitting off the last factor).
questions.source_support: The definition expresses $n!$ as the product of all positive natural numbers up to $n$.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
option_explanations: n! = n + (n-1)! uses addition, not multiplication.
n! = (n-1)!/n divides instead of multiplying.
From the product $n!=1\cdot 2\cdots (n-1)\cdot n$, splitting off the last factor gives $n!=n\cdot(n-1)!$; $n^2=n\cdot n$ keeps only two copies of $n$ and drops the intervening factors $2,\dots,n-1$.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
